 Closings and Delays Michigan warns of Medicare scams during open enrollment 
 State says scammers are seeking Medicare numbers and private information ahead of enrollment deadline 
 The state of Michigan says scammers are using the Medicare enrollment period to get people’s Medicare numbers and other private information. By Taryn Hostetter Published : Nov. 6, 2026 at 4:45 AM EST | Updated : 4 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google LANSING, Mich. (News 10) - The state of Michigan says scammers are using the Medicare enrollment period to get people’s Medicare numbers and other private information.
 How the scams reach people
 The state says Medicare scams are not limited to phone calls. They also can come by mail or an unsolicited knock at the door, with people asking for personal information.
 Keaton James, who works for American Senior Benefits, said people should be wary while speaking with unknown callers.
 “People are getting phone calls right now that are, you know, less than honest. Maybe looking to switch their plan without their consent. Or just get personal health information from them that they otherwise shouldn’t give them,” James said.
 James said no one who is licensed and works legitimately is allowed to say they are from Medicare or endorsed by Medicare.
 “Nobody that is licensed that does this legitimately is allowed to say that they’re from Medicare or endorsed by Medicare or anything like that. And so if you hear those things, you’re probably talking to a scammer,” James said.
 Where to get free help
 For free help, the state points people to MI Options counselors. MI Options is Michigan’s free Medicare enrollment hotline. People can also go through an agent for enrollment help.
 James said both options can help people avoid high-pressure sales pitches and signing up for something they might not want.
 “You know, we do this all day, every day. And so we’re just here to help,” James said.
 James said people should pay attention to how the conversation feels while getting help during Medicare enrollment, and should make sure an agent fits their needs before choosing one.
 “It should feel like a collaborative, like safe space to sit and talk to your agent. It should not feel salesy or pressuring. You know, it should feel like you’re being educated and informed,” James said.
 What to do before signing up
 With the use of AI, scams are sounding like real agents looking to help people enroll. Before signing up for anything, people should take their time. The state says to never share a Medicare number with anyone who makes first contact.
 How to report
 People who think they have been targeted can report it to Michigan’s Department of Insurance and Financial Services. To file a fraud report, call 877-999-6442.
 The Medicare enrollment deadline is Dec. 7.
